paragraphs: A gaze estimation model trained in one setting may perform poorly in another because the relationship between its training data and target data changes. This paper argues that learning features that look similar across domains is insufficient under the generalized label shift perspective. It instead treats transfer as a combination of changes in gaze labels and changes in conditional distributions.

The proposed correction framework first adjusts the importance of source examples to account for differences in label distributions. Gaze labels are continuous, which makes this correction harder than assigning weights to a small collection of categories. The authors introduce a weighting strategy based on a truncated Gaussian distribution to address that difficulty.

They then incorporate the reweighted source distribution into conditional invariant learning through a probability-aware estimate of conditional operator discrepancy. This connects label correction with the effort to align conditional relationships across domains. Experiments on standard cross-domain gaze tasks and multiple backbone models report stronger generalization, supporting the framework’s usefulness across the evaluated model architectures.
neurips-2025-a-generalized-label-shift-p.tldr: The paper improves cross-domain gaze estimation by correcting label-distribution differences alongside conditional differences between domains.

paragraphs: Two-layer neural networks trained from very small initial weights can learn in bursts: progress appears slow before the loss suddenly drops. Alternating Gradient Flows explains this pattern through an approximation that separates the search for useful features from the strengthening of features already acquired. Its starting point treats every neuron as dormant, corresponding to initialization at the origin.

The framework alternates between maximizing a utility function for dormant neurons and minimizing a cost for active neurons. Activating a neuron represents acquiring a feature and produces a loss decrease. This description predicts the order, timing, and size of those decreases, with experimental agreement across several studied architectures.

The theoretical results have distinct scopes. For diagonal linear networks, the authors prove convergence to gradient flow as initialization vanishes. The framework also extends earlier analyses of fully connected linear networks and attention-only linear transformers. For quadratic networks learning modular addition, it characterizes the full training dynamics and shows Fourier features emerging in descending coefficient magnitude. Together, these results make feature acquisition more explicit in the analyzed settings.
neurips-2025-alternating-gradient-flows-.tldr: Alternating Gradient Flows explains staged feature learning in several two-layer network settings by alternating neuron activation and active-feature optimization.

paragraphs: A coreset compresses a dataset while approximately preserving the optimization costs that matter. This paper studies summaries for the robust geometric median, where a specified number of observations can be treated as outliers. The summary must approximate the robust cost for every candidate center within a multiplicative error controlled by epsilon.

For n data points and m outliers, the main construction removes the earlier linear dependence on m when n is at least four times m. Its size is approximately epsilon to the minus two times the smaller of epsilon to the minus two and dimension d, with logarithmic factors suppressed. The one-dimensional case has a separate optimal bound that still includes the outlier fraction m/n.

The technical advance analyzes approximation error jointly rather than component by component, reducing the influence of outliers on summary size. Extensions remove dependence on the outlier count for broader robust clustering problems under mild data assumptions. Experiments report better size–accuracy tradeoffs and runtime, including datasets violating those assumptions; these empirical results are broader than the stated theoretical conditions.
neurips-2025-coreset-for-robust-geometri.tldr: A new error analysis yields robust geometric-median coresets whose main size bound avoids dependence on the outlier count when n ≥ 4m.

paragraphs: Scheduling computing workloads across distant data centers involves changing electricity prices, carbon intensity, weather, and network conditions. DCcluster-Opt provides a simulation benchmark that brings these factors together with models of computing hardware and cooling. Its purpose is to make scheduling strategies comparable under a richer account of operational tradeoffs.

The benchmark combines real-world workload traces and environmental data with physics-informed models. Its inputs cover weather across 20 global regions, electricity markets, grid emissions, transmission costs, and empirical network delays. A coordinating agent chooses whether to move or defer incoming tasks across a configurable group of data centers while accounting for their resource needs and service-level requirements.

A modular reward system lets researchers explicitly examine competing objectives involving emissions, energy costs, service commitments, and water consumption. The environment also includes components such as heat recovery. A Gymnasium interface and reinforcement-learning and rule-based controllers support reproducible comparisons. The contribution is an open-source testbed for developing and evaluating scheduling methods, with realistic interactions represented inside a configurable simulation.
neurips-2025-dccluster-opt-benchmarking-.tldr: DCcluster-Opt simulates geographically distributed data centers so scheduling methods can be compared across environmental, cost, and service objectives.

paragraphs: Training language models to reconstruct readable source code from compiled binaries requires trustworthy examples linking the two. Those links are difficult to establish because compilation settings and function inlining can obscure the original function boundaries. Decompile-Bench addresses this data problem with a large collection drawn from permissively licensed GitHub projects.

The dataset contains two million binary–source function pairs selected from 100 million collected pairs, associated with 450GB of compiled binaries. The goal is to provide more realistic function-level correspondence than contest-style tasks, synthetic mappings, or matches limited to code lines and variable names. Such correspondence matters because a decompiler must recover a function’s behavior from its compiled representation.

The authors also create Decompile-Bench-Eval using manually crafted binaries from HumanEval and MBPP together with compiled repositories released after 2025 to mitigate leakage. They examine commonly used evaluation measures and report a 20% improvement in re-executability rate from fine-tuning with Decompile-Bench compared with previous benchmarks. This finding supports the training value of the dataset on an execution-oriented measure.
neurips-2025-decompile-bench-million-sca.tldr: Decompile-Bench supplies two million binary–source function pairs and reports improved re-executability after decompiler fine-tuning.

paragraphs: World models let agents imagine future states when learning how to act. Long sequences of imagined states are difficult because errors in individual predictions can accumulate. This paper targets that problem in recurrent state-space models by adding a reasoning component intended to keep imagined trajectories logically consistent with the environment.

DMWM divides the work between two interacting systems, inspired by dual-process accounts of human cognition. System 1 uses a recurrent state-space model to handle state transitions. System 2 uses a logic-integrated neural network to guide imagination through hierarchical reasoning. Feedback between them is designed to make the imagined sequence follow the environment’s logical rules.

This arrangement connects prediction of the next state with guidance over the longer imagined process. The authors evaluate it on tasks requiring extended planning in DMControl and a robotic environment. They report significant improvements over state-of-the-art world models in logical coherence, trial efficiency, data efficiency, and long-term imagination. Those findings support the proposed combination as a way to improve planning-related imagination in the tested environments.
neurips-2025-dmwm-dual-mind-world-model-.tldr: DMWM combines recurrent state prediction with logical reasoning to improve long-term imagination and planning efficiency in evaluated control tasks.

paragraphs: Tracking multiple objects requires recognizing the same individuals across video frames, even when appearances change or detections become unreliable. Updating an object’s representation helps follow its current appearance, but tracking also needs stable information about its identity. This paper builds an end-to-end transformer framework that gives these responsibilities separate decoder paths.

The appearance path updates query features using the current frame. The identity path keeps query features fixed and reuses historical sampling offsets to preserve longer-term consistency. This separation allows the model to represent changing visual evidence while retaining stable identity cues. A confidence-guided rule further suppresses updates when predictions are unreliable, keeping features that were previously trustworthy.

The design directly addresses the instability associated with occlusions, appearance changes, and missed detections. Experiments on multiple-object-tracking benchmarks report state-of-the-art results across major tracking measures, with particularly strong gains in association accuracy and identity consistency. The stated findings support separating appearance adaptation from identity preservation as a useful architectural choice for robust tracking in the evaluated complex scenarios.
neurips-2025-dual-path-temporal-decoder-.tldr: A dual-path tracking decoder separately updates appearance and preserves identity, improving object associations across video frames.

paragraphs: Machine unlearning tries to remove unwanted information from a trained model while retaining useful capabilities. Treating forgetting and utility as two competing objectives can produce a Pareto-optimal compromise without giving precise control over how much forgetting occurs. This paper instead places the unlearning objective first, subject to a bound on the increase in utility loss.

The authors show that solving this constrained problem is equivalent to applying unilateral gradient surgery to the unlearning objective. In this formulation, the allowed damage to utility explicitly shapes how the forgetting update is adjusted. The constraint therefore provides a more directed way to manage the tradeoff than merely seeking some compromise between the two objectives.

Because explicit gradient surgery introduces computational overhead, the proposed method approximates the constrained solution implicitly using a single backpropagation. The paper provides a tight convergence analysis and reports better forgetting–utility tradeoffs than existing baselines in extensive experiments. Its contribution combines a clearer optimization target with an efficient approximation, while retaining the distinction between the exact constrained formulation and the practical update.
neurips-2025-efficient-utility-preservin.tldr: Implicit gradient surgery efficiently approximates unlearning updates that prioritize forgetting while limiting increases in utility loss.

paragraphs: Federated learning must make progress with limited communication while handling clients whose data distributions differ. Momentum can accelerate training, and sharpness-aware minimization encourages flatter solutions. This paper identifies two problems with combining them directly: local perturbation directions may misrepresent the global loss geometry, and accumulated momentum can destabilize later training.

FedWMSAM uses momentum aggregated at the server to construct a shared perturbation that guides clients toward the global descent geometry. This also enables an approximation to sharpness-aware minimization using one backpropagation. An adaptive rule based on cosine similarity couples the two mechanisms, producing a schedule that emphasizes momentum early and sharpness-aware training later.

The theoretical analysis provides a convergence bound for non-identically distributed client data and explicitly accounts for extra variance introduced by perturbations. That matters because the mechanism used to encourage flatness also changes optimization noise. Experiments across datasets and architectures report effectiveness, adaptability, and robustness. The contribution is therefore a coordinated treatment of acceleration and flatness that directly targets the two identified failure modes.
neurips-2025-fedwmsam-fast-and-flat-fede.tldr: FedWMSAM coordinates global momentum and sharpness-aware updates to address misalignment and late-training instability in federated learning.

paragraphs: Repeated language-model workflows often reuse the same request structure while changing details that affect the answer. Exact-match caching misses these opportunities because the prompts differ. Semantic caching can make the opposite mistake: treating similar requests as interchangeable even when a small difference is important to the required response.

GenCache approaches reuse by identifying response patterns associated with similar prompt structures. It then synthesizes an output customized to the new request. The reusable element is therefore a response pattern that can accommodate variation. This matters for recurring workflows because structural similarity can remain useful even when simply returning an earlier answer would be incorrect.

The reported evaluation reaches an 83% cache hit rate with minimal incorrect hits on datasets containing no prompt repetition. In agentic workflows, GenCache improves cache hit rate by approximately 20% and reduces end-to-end execution latency by approximately 34% relative to standard prompt matching. These findings indicate that adapting cached patterns can expand useful reuse and shorten execution in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-generative-caching-for-stru.tldr: GenCache customizes reusable response patterns for structurally similar prompts, increasing cache hits and reducing evaluated workflow latency.

paragraphs: Giving a reasoning model more computation at inference time can involve an external reward model that evaluates its answers. This paper finds only marginal gains from that approach for models already post-trained on particular reasoning tasks. The authors attribute the limitation to a distribution mismatch between the specialized answer generator and the more general reward model.

Their proposed framework trains one model to both produce answers and assess their correctness. Generation and verification are combined within a single reinforcement-learning process. The resulting model can use its own verification capability during inference, allowing additional computation to improve answer selection without depending on a separate external verifier.

The authors train models based on Qwen2.5-Math-7B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and examine different reasoning context lengths. Across multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks, they report improvements both after training and when scaling inference-time computation. The results support learning verification alongside generation as a way to make the evaluator better matched to the model’s own solutions in these reasoning settings.
neurips-2025-incentivizing-llms-to-self-.tldr: Joint reinforcement learning of answer generation and self-verification improves mathematical reasoning and enables inference-time scaling without external verifiers.

paragraphs: Human movement reflects goals as well as physical motion. The paper argues that datasets centered on short actions in static settings provide too little context for learning why someone moves. Intend to Move addresses this gap by connecting motion recordings with the surrounding environment, another person, and descriptions of intentions as they evolve.

The dataset contains 10.1 hours of two-person 3D motion sequences captured in realistic, changing home environments. It pairs those sequences with video and depth from multiple viewpoints, 3D scene geometry, and language annotations of each participant’s intentions. These complementary records make goals, physical surroundings, and social context available together for motion modeling.

Benchmark experiments expose a gap in current models: they struggle to turn high-level goals into motion that is coherent both physically and socially. This makes the dataset useful as an evaluation resource as well as training material. The intended research direction is motion understanding that connects prediction and action to a person’s purpose, with the benchmark revealing where current systems fall short.
neurips-2025-intend-to-move-a-multimodal.tldr: Intend to Move links two-person motion, home environments, and evolving intentions to benchmark goal-aware human motion modeling.

paragraphs: Panoptic scene completion reconstructs a 3D scene with both semantic categories and distinctions between individual objects. This extends scene understanding beyond identifying what occupies a location to identifying which object it belongs to. IPFormer studies this task using camera images, a setting the abstract describes as comparatively unexplored.

The method focuses on the queries used to reconstruct objects. Earlier transformer approaches begin with learned queries that remain fixed at test time, limiting their initial adaptation to the particular scene. IPFormer instead derives instance proposals from the image context during both training and testing. Attention-based encoding and decoding then refine these proposals to reason about relationships between object instances and scene voxels.

Starting from scene-dependent proposals gives the reconstruction process information specific to the observed image. The authors report state-of-the-art performance on in-domain data, stronger zero-shot generalization to out-of-domain data, and a runtime reduction exceeding 14 times. These results support context-adaptive initialization as a useful design choice for the evaluated camera-based 3D panoptic completion tasks.
neurips-2025-ipformer-visual-3d-panoptic.tldr: IPFormer uses image-dependent object proposals to improve camera-based 3D panoptic scene completion, generalization, and runtime.

paragraphs: Visual tracking requires estimating where target pixels move and whether they remain visible. The Lattice Boltzmann Model represents this changing visual information through dynamic pixel lattices. It uses collision and streaming processes to model motion states, organizing tracking around interactions in space and movement through time.

A multilayer predict–update network estimates a high-dimensional distribution over target pixels. In the prediction stage, lattice collisions describe interactions among nearby target pixels, while lattice streaming uses temporal visual context. The update stage corrects those distributions with visual representations obtained online. This repeatedly connects motion predictions with incoming observations when estimating positions and visibility.

The authors emphasize online, real-time operation as a practical feature of the approach. Evaluations on TAP-Vid and RoboTAP support its efficiency for point tracking, while experiments on TAO, BFT, and OVT-B examine broader open-world object tracking. Together, these evaluations support the proposed motion representation’s practicality across the tested point- and object-tracking settings, connecting the lattice formulation to tasks involving real-world visual changes.
neurips-2025-lattice-boltzmann-model-for.tldr: The Lattice Boltzmann Model uses spatial collision, temporal streaming, and online correction to track pixel positions and visibility in real time.

paragraphs: Estimating lighting from an image or video requires recovering illumination that is only indirectly visible through its effects on the scene. The output must also represent a wide range of brightness values. LuxDiT tackles this problem by adapting a video diffusion transformer to generate high-dynamic-range environment maps conditioned on visual input.

Training data is a central obstacle because measured HDR environment maps are expensive to collect and lack diversity. The authors train on a large synthetic dataset spanning varied lighting conditions. This teaches the model to connect indirect visual cues with illumination, and the paper reports effective generalization to real scenes. The method thus uses synthetic diversity to support lighting inference from observed appearance.

A further low-rank adaptation stage uses collected HDR panoramas to improve semantic alignment between the input and predicted lighting map. The reported outputs contain realistic fine angular details alongside accurate lighting predictions. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations outperform existing state-of-the-art methods, supporting the combination of generative modeling, synthetic training, and panorama-based adaptation for the evaluated lighting-estimation tasks.
neurips-2025-luxdit-lighting-estimation-.tldr: LuxDiT adapts a video diffusion transformer with synthetic lighting data and HDR panoramas to estimate detailed scene illumination.

paragraphs: Some decisions require a probability distribution over several related outputs, conditioned on observed inputs. A poorly calibrated joint distribution can make those predictions unreliable. Existing recalibration methods mostly address individual outputs, while multivariate conformal prediction supplies coverage regions without explicitly specifying the full probability distribution inside and outside those regions.

This paper introduces latent calibration for conditional invertible generative models, including normalizing flows and flow matching. It evaluates calibration in the model’s latent representation. The proposed latent recalibration method then learns a transformation of that space after the original model has been trained, producing a revised distribution with an explicit multivariate density.

The method includes finite-sample bounds on latent calibration and is designed to remain computationally efficient. Experiments on tabular and image datasets consistently improve both latent calibration error and negative log-likelihood. These findings support correcting probability models through their latent spaces while retaining a usable density. The theoretical bounds concern the introduced latent-calibration notion, and the reported empirical improvements also address how well the recalibrated models assign probability to observed data.
neurips-2025-multivariate-latent-recalib.tldr: Latent recalibration adjusts a trained generative model’s latent space to improve multivariate probabilistic calibration while preserving an explicit density.

paragraphs: Open Vision Reasoner investigates how reasoning behaviors developed through language can support reasoning about visual inputs. Built on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, it uses a large linguistic cold-start training phase followed by nearly 1,000 steps of multimodal reinforcement learning. The study examines both the resulting performance and how useful behaviors develop across these stages.

The authors report that behavior transfer appears early in cold-start training, which they attribute to linguistic mental imagery. They distinguish the roles of the stages: cold start broadly memorizes visual behaviors, while reinforcement learning identifies effective patterns and amplifies them. Transfer also favors behaviors with high utility, including visual reflection, rather than strengthening all behaviors equally.

The resulting model achieves reported state-of-the-art performance across a suite of reasoning benchmarks, with scores of 95.3% on MATH500, 51.8% on MathVision, and 54.6% on MathVerse. Alongside these results, the paper contributes an account of how language-based preparation and multimodal reinforcement interact. The released model, data, and training dynamics make that training approach available for further study.
neurips-2025-open-vision-reasoner-transf.tldr: Open Vision Reasoner transfers language-based reasoning behaviors through cold-start training and strengthens effective visual behaviors with multimodal reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Driving world models need to generate plausible futures over extended periods, including difficult situations such as turns and urban traffic. This paper develops a model using simple design choices without extra supervision or sensors such as maps, depth, or multiple cameras. It reports state-of-the-art performance with 469 million parameters and training on 280 hours of video.

A central part of the study compares two ways to model the visual sequence: discrete tokens and continuous representations based on flow matching. To make a side-by-side comparison possible, the authors construct a hybrid tokenizer compatible with both approaches. This provides a shared representation mechanism for investigating whether discrete-token modeling offers an advantage.

The study instead favors the continuous autoregressive model. In the reported comparison, it is more capable and less sensitive to individual design choices than the discrete-token model. Its particularly strong performance on turning maneuvers and urban traffic connects that conclusion to challenging driving scenarios. The contribution combines an effective video-based world model with evidence about representation and generation choices within the evaluated setup.
neurips-2025-overcoming-challenges-of-lo.tldr: A video-based driving world model achieves strong long-horizon results, with a shared-tokenizer comparison favoring continuous autoregressive generation.

paragraphs: Partial information decomposition asks how multiple sources inform a target: what each contributes uniquely, what they repeat, and what becomes informative only when combined. Applying it to continuous, high-dimensional data is difficult because existing methods optimize over a joint distribution subject to estimated pairwise distributions, which can be costly and inaccurate.

The paper develops an efficient approach for the case where the pairwise distributions are multivariate Gaussian. An alternative optimization formulation leads to a new gradient-based algorithm for this Gaussian PID problem. To address non-Gaussian inputs, the authors learn information-preserving encoders that transform variables into representations with pairwise Gaussian distributions. They also resolve an open question about the optimality of joint Gaussian solutions.

Tests on diverse synthetic examples report more accurate and efficient estimates than existing baselines. Evaluations on large multimodal benchmarks further demonstrate uses in measuring information relationships and selecting high-performing models. The approach matters because it connects a computationally tractable distributional setting with learned representations, extending the practical reach of decomposition to the evaluated multimodal data.
neurips-2025-partial-information-decompo.tldr: The paper combines efficient Gaussian partial information decomposition with learned encoders to estimate unique, redundant, and synergistic multimodal information.

paragraphs: Generating audio as a stream requires producing sound with little delay. Conditional flow matching improves sampling efficiency, but its repeated sampling steps remain an obstacle for this setting. StreamFlow adapts the generative process specifically for real-time audio reconstruction from discrete tokens, making streaming behavior part of the training design.

The method uses causal noising along the time axis and predicts vector fields for multiple times together on each stream. This arrangement enables low-latency streaming inference. The authors also introduce Scale-DiT, a diffusion transformer that models, normalizes, and scales feature differences before skip connections. This architectural change improves robustness and performance without increasing the number of parameters.

Audio reconstruction experiments use discrete tokens produced by EnCodec and Mimi, demonstrating high-fidelity synthesis alongside streaming capability. The authors additionally integrate StreamFlow into Moshi’s fully duplex streaming speech language models by replacing the Mimi decoder. That integration shows the method functioning as an audio-generation component within a streaming speech system, extending the evidence beyond standalone reconstruction tasks.
neurips-2025-streamflow-streaming-audio-.tldr: StreamFlow combines causal flow-matching training and a revised diffusion transformer to generate high-fidelity audio streams from discrete tokens.

paragraphs: Vision language models appear easy to jailbreak, yet some defenses obtain nearly saturated benchmark scores with little effort. This paper investigates that apparent contradiction. It analyzes the inclusion of visual inputs as a tentative explanation for vulnerability, while also examining whether strong defense scores reflect dependable behavior on both harmful and benign requests.

A central finding is over-prudence: defenses may abstain even when inputs are harmless. Such behavior can make a defense look successful at blocking attacks while reducing its usefulness on legitimate requests. The authors propose LLM-Pipeline, a detector used before the vision language model responds that repurposes the more developed guardrails of language-only models.

The paper also finds that two representative jailbreak evaluation methods often agree only at chance level. This makes assessments of attack and defense quality potentially misleading. Together, the findings connect the paradox to input vulnerability, excessive refusal, and unreliable evaluation. The proposed detector provides an alternative defense mechanism, while the analysis motivates reconsidering how safety benchmarks distinguish protection from unnecessary abstention.
neurips-2025-the-vllm-safety-paradox-dua.tldr: The paper links strong-looking vision-model defenses to excessive refusal and unreliable evaluation, and proposes a language-model-based safety detector.

paragraphs: Explicit reasoning chains can improve language-model answers, but generating every reasoning token is expensive. CoLaR trains a model to reason using compressed latent representations, allowing multiple consecutive token embeddings to be merged. Its compression factor can be specified at inference time, giving users a way to adjust the compactness of reasoning.

During supervised training, an auxiliary objective teaches a specialized latent head to predict distributions of subsequent compressed embeddings. Compression factors are randomly sampled from a predefined range. Reinforcement learning then uses the head’s stochastic predictions to explore different reasoning paths and favor more compact ones, connecting compression with learned reasoning behavior.

Across four mathematical datasets, CoLaR reports 14.1% higher accuracy than latent baselines at comparable compression ratios. Compared with explicit chain-of-thought reasoning, it shortens chains by 53.3% with 4.8% performance degradation. On harder mathematical tasks, the reinforcement-enhanced version reports gains up to 5.4% while reducing latent chain length by 82.8%. These comparisons show different accuracy–length tradeoffs; the results do not imply that every compression setting preserves performance.
neurips-2025-think-silently-think-fast-d.tldr: CoLaR learns compressed latent reasoning with an adjustable compression factor, achieving shorter mathematical reasoning chains with measured accuracy tradeoffs.

paragraphs: Reasoning about video requires connecting visual evidence with events, timing, and causal relationships. VideoRFT applies a two-stage training process to this challenge: supervised learning from annotated reasoning chains, followed by reinforcement learning intended to improve generalization. A central obstacle is obtaining enough high-quality reasoning annotations grounded in the actual videos.

The authors build a curation pipeline in which a reasoning language model first drafts chains from rich, structured, literal descriptions of video content. A multimodal model then revises those drafts while viewing the video. This second pass checks visual consistency and reduces hallucinations. The pipeline produces VideoRFT-CoT-102K for supervised training and VideoRFT-RL-310K for reinforcement learning.

During reinforcement learning, a semantic-consistency reward explicitly encourages agreement between textual reasoning and visual evidence. This makes grounding part of the optimization objective as well as the annotation process. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance on six video reasoning benchmarks. The results support combining curated reasoning examples with a reward that encourages the model’s explanations to remain connected to what the video shows.
neurips-2025-videorft-incentivizing-vide.tldr: VideoRFT combines video-grounded reasoning data and a semantic-consistency reward to improve multimodal video reasoning.

paragraphs: An intervention can change more than an immediate outcome: it can also change how the system responds to later interventions. This paper studies settings where causal relationships themselves evolve. Under those conditions, treating repeated interventions as having stable effects can make a static average treatment effect insufficient or misleading.

The authors build on meta-causal models, which support reasoning about changing causal relationships. They propose a particular class of these models with properties intended to support explicit modeling and prediction of intervention outcomes under such dynamics. They also introduce a method for meta-causal analysis, moving from qualitative recognition of evolving relationships toward analyzing interventions within the proposed framework.

Expository examples concern medical treatment and judicial decision-making. They illustrate serious consequences of neglecting system dynamics and demonstrate how meta-causal strategies can navigate the modeled situations. The contribution is a framework and analysis method for interventions that may reshape their own future effects. The examples establish the intended reasoning use cases, rather than reporting clinical or judicial deployment outcomes.
neurips-2025-when-causal-dynamics-matter.tldr: The paper develops meta-causal models and an analysis method for interventions that can change a system’s underlying causal relationships.

paragraphs: Predicting learning curves can help decide how much training and data collection are needed to reach a performance goal. This paper treats curve prediction as a multitask learning problem, organizing each task’s data within a two-level hierarchy. The aim is to share evidence across related tasks and reduce the cost of constructing scaling laws.

The model uses latent-variable, multi-output Gaussian processes to represent dependencies between tasks and hierarchical levels. This supports zero-shot prediction of learning curves while expressing uncertainty about those predictions. An active-learning strategy can then query curves to reduce uncertainty, making additional observations useful for refining the predicted scaling relationships.

The authors report predictions close to ground-truth scaling laws when using this querying strategy. Validation covers three small-scale NLP datasets with up to 30 learning curves, involving nanoGPT, bilingual translation with mBART and Transformers, and multilingual translation with different-sized M2M100 models. That scope supports the approach’s feasibility for the studied settings: related curves can inform new predictions, and targeted queries can improve them without exhaustively observing every curve.
neurips-2025-zero-shot-performance-predi.tldr: A hierarchical Gaussian-process framework predicts learning curves across related NLP tasks and uses active learning to reduce scaling-law uncertainty.
